## Comparability caveat

Two limitations before the numbers:

1. **Alaska's FY2024 is not a clean, like-for-like period.** Alaska completed its acquisition of Hawaiian Holdings on September 18, 2024, and "the results of Hawaiian are included in the consolidated financial statements beginning September 18, 2024," contributing "$869 million" of revenue and a "$113 million" net loss in that stub period [DOC-2]. So Alaska's FY2024 blends ~8.5 months of standalone Alaska with ~3.5 months of a larger, loss-making combined entity, plus likely merger-related costs. Its ratios are not strictly comparable to the four organic full-year filers.
2. **No unit-cost (CASM/ASM) data is available in the source.** The excerpts provide only dollar amounts [DOC-1], so "efficiency" here must be measured as cost-to-revenue ratios and operating margin, not cost per available seat mile — the airline industry's standard efficiency metric. Cost-to-revenue ratios are also influenced by pricing/revenue premium, not cost discipline alone.

## Comparison (all calendar-year FY2024, $M) [DOC-1]

| Airline | Revenue | Fuel | Labor | Fuel+Labor % of Rev | Operating margin |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Delta | $61,643 | $10,566 | $16,161 | **43.4%** | **9.7%** |
| United | $57,063 | $11,756 | $16,678 | 49.8% | 8.9% |
| American | $54,211 | $11,418 | $16,021 | 50.6% | 4.8% |
| Alaska* | $11,735 | $2,506 | $3,588 | 51.9% | 4.9% |
| Southwest | $27,483 | $5,812 | $12,240 | 65.7% | 1.2% |

\*partial-year Hawaiian inclusion [DOC-2]

## Assessment

Delta leads on both measures: fuel of $10,566M and salaries of $16,161M against $61,643M of revenue — the lowest combined cost ratio at 43.4% — and the highest operating margin, $5,995M on $61,643M, or 9.7% [DOC-1]. United is second (28,434/57,063 = 49.8%; 5,096/57,063 = 8.9%) [DOC-1].

Southwest is clearly the weakest: labor alone consumes 44.5% of revenue ($12,240M on $27,483M), and operating income of just $321M yields a 1.2% margin [DOC-1]. American ($2,614M on $54,211M = 4.8%) and Alaska ($570M on $11,735M = 4.9%) sit in the middle, with Alaska's figure carrying the acquisition-distortion caveat above [DOC-1][DOC-2].

Note that Delta's advantage is partly a revenue-premium effect (highest revenue base absorbing fixed costs), not purely lower unit costs; a CASM-based answer could differ.

ANSWER: Delta Air Lines — lowest combined fuel+labor cost ratio (43.4% of revenue) and highest operating margin (9.7%); Southwest was least efficient (65.7%; 1.2% margin). Alaska's figures are not fully comparable due to the mid-year Hawaiian acquisition.
